items.description: Credit scoring models trained on historical data may encode systemic biases against protected groups (age, gender, ethnicity). Article 9(9) requires consideration of impacts on vulnerable groups.

mitigations.description: Apply the release gate on demographic parity and equal opportunity difference (above 0.10 blocks release) by sex, age band and foreign worker flag.
mitigations.recorded_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk

items.title: Demographic bias in credit scoring outputs

items.description: Where a solely automated credit decision falls under GDPR Article 22(2)(a) or (c), GDPR Article 22(3) gives at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision, and GDPR Articles 13(2)(f), 14(2)(g) and 15(1)(h) require meaningful information about the logic involved. The system may not currently support this.

mitigations.description: Return the four inputs that contributed most to each score as reason codes, for the lender to pass to the applicant on request.

items.description: GDPR Article 22(1) gives a right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects the person. GDPR Articles 13(2)(f), 14(2)(g) and 15(1)(h) require meaningful information about the logic involved. An explanation capability is a key technical control.

items.description: Article 9(6) and (8) require testing against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds appropriate to the intended purpose. Article 15(5) covers resilience against adversarial examples.

mitigations.description: Before release, test on a recent sample of the lender's own applicants with amounts converted from DM to euro, plus edge cases (extreme amount and duration) and small input perturbations; the cost-weighted error must not exceed the hold-out value by more than 10 percent.
mitigations.recorded_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk

items.title: Has the system been tested against out-of-distribution inputs, edge cases, and adversarial perturbations?

items.description: Aggregate metrics can mask poor performance for subpopulations. Slice-level evaluation is required for high-risk systems.

mitigations.description: Report accuracy, precision, recall, calibration error and cost under the dataset's cost matrix (5 for a bad applicant scored good, 1 for the reverse) per subgroup on the hold-out set.
mitigations.recorded_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk

items.title: Are accuracy, precision, recall, and calibration metrics documented across all relevant demographic subgroups?

items.description: A defined performance floor ensures degraded models do not remain in production. This is a key operational control.

items.description: Models degrade over time as real-world data distributions shift. Post-market monitoring under Article 72 requires detection and response.

mitigations.description: Retrain on recent applicant data from the lender before release, and do not put the model trained only on the 1994 records into production.
mitigations.recorded_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk

mitigations.description: Compute the population stability index of every input and of the score each month; above 0.25 the lender is alerted and the model is reviewed within 30 days.
mitigations.recorded_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk

items.acceptance_rationale: The creator, DOI, licence and file dates are recorded, but when, where and from whom the 1994 records were collected is not published and cannot be recovered. The gap is stated in the limitations section, and the model is retrained on recent lender data before release, so the remaining provenance gap is accepted.
items.accepted_by: Mara Lindqvist, Head of Model Risk
items.description: Article 10(2) requires data governance practices including documentation of dataset provenance. TraceForge can automate this.
items.title: Is the provenance of all training, validation, and test datasets documented (source, collection date, license, version)?

items.description: Article 10(3) requires training, validation and testing data sets to be, to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose. Article 10(2)(c) covers data-preparation processing operations such as cleaning.
items.title: Are data quality checks (completeness, consistency, accuracy) applied and documented before training and fine-tuning?

items.description: Data retained beyond its purpose creates ongoing legal and privacy risk. GDPR Article 5(1)(e) requires storage limitation.
items.title: Is there a data retention and deletion schedule that covers both training data and inference logs?

system.name: Retail Credit Risk Scorer
system.purpose: Credit scoring of retail consumer credit applicants: a binary classifier, trained on the UCI Statlog German Credit data, scores each applicant as good or bad credit risk, and a lender's credit officer uses the score when deciding on the application.
